stem: In a code language, letters at odd positions in a word (1st, 3rd, 5th) are shifted 2 places forward in the alphabet, while letters at even positions (2nd, 4th) are shifted 2 places backward. For example, DIGIT is coded as FGIGV. Using this rule, what is the code for FORCE?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Odd positions +2, even positions -2: F(1,odd)+2=H, O(2,even)-2=M, R(3,odd)+2=T, C(4,even)-2=A, E(5,odd)+2=G, giving HMTAG.
Applying +2 to all positions regardless of odd/even gives HQTEG, ignoring the -2 rule for even positions.
Applying -2 to all positions regardless of odd/even gives DMPAC, ignoring the +2 rule for odd positions.
Reversing the rule (odd positions -2, even positions +2) gives F-2=D, O+2=Q, R-2=P, C+2=E, E-2=C, producing DQPEC.

explanation: The rule applies a position-dependent shift: odd word-positions shift +2, even word-positions shift -2. Verify with DIGIT: D(1,odd)+2=F, I(2,even)-2=G, G(3,odd)+2=I, I(4,even)-2=G, T(5,odd)+2=V = FGIGV (matches). Apply to FORCE: F(pos1)+2=H, O(pos2)-2=M, R(pos3)+2=T, C(pos4)-2=A, E(pos5)+2=G = HMTAG.

explanation_sections.punchline: The setup decision is recognising which positions get +2 and which get -2 - the two most common wrong answers flip or ignore this split.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: re-verify the example first (DIGIT->FGIGV), explicitly noting the odd/even alternation, then map each letter of FORCE with its position tag before coding.
explanation_sections.lesson: With position-dependent coding rules, always tag each letter with its position number (1,2,3...) before applying the shift to avoid flip errors.
explanation_sections.timing: About 70-80 seconds. Fastest elimination: option 2 (HQTEG) has O+2=Q which requires all even positions to use +2, contradicting the example where I(pos2) maps to G (I-2=G).
